proposals.before: In the fourth year (569), Northern Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; bandits killed Kongcheng garrison commander Neng Benda, who fled to the enemy and yielded the city to them.
proposals.after: In the fourth year (569), Northern Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; bandits killed Kongcheng garrison commander Neng Benda, and the city went over to them.
proposals.reason: 能奔達 is the personal name of the garrison commander; 盜殺 records his killing. The English wrongly treats 奔達 as a verb of flight, making a dead man also flee and surrender the city.

proposals.before: Year 4, Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; bandits killed Kongcheng garrison commander Neng Benda, who fled and reached them, yielding the city to them.
proposals.after: Year 4, Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; bandits killed Kongcheng garrison commander Neng Benda, and the city went over to them.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise misreads 能奔達 as 'able to flee and reach' instead of the name, contradicting 盜殺.

proposals.before: Northern Qi general Prince of Xincai Wang Kangde, when Yuwen Xian's army arrived, quietly withdrew his force by night.
proposals.after: Northern Qi general Prince of Xincai Wang Kang, learning that Yuwen Xian's troops had arrived, quietly withdrew his force by night.
proposals.reason: Chinese 新蔡王王康得以憲兵至 names 王康; 得以 belongs to the clause ‘when/learning that Xian’s troops arrived,’ not a given name Kangde.

proposals.before: Qi general Prince of Xincai Wang Kangde, when Xian's army arrived, quietly withdrew his force by night.
proposals.after: Qi general Prince of Xincai Wang Kang, when Xian's army arrived, quietly withdrew his force by night.
proposals.reason: Literal English fuses 王康 with 得以 into the false personal name Wang Kangde.

proposals.before: Yuwen Xian had Pillar-of-State Tan Gonghui build Shidian city as relief for Fen Province.
proposals.after: Yuwen Xian had Pillar-of-State Hui, Duke of Tan, build Shidian city as relief for Fen Province.
proposals.reason: 柱國、譚公會 is the office plus the title 譚公 and given name 會, not a trisyllabic surname-name Tan Gonghui.

proposals.before: Xian had Pillar-of-State Tan Gonghui build Shidian city as relief for Fen Province.
proposals.after: Xian had Pillar-of-State Hui, Duke of Tan, build Shidian city as relief for Fen Province.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise treats 譚公會 as a single personal name instead of Duke of Tan, Hui.

proposals.before: High Ancestor: "You shall be the forward army; I too shall follow in dispatch."
proposals.after: High Ancestor said: "You shall be the forward army; I too shall follow in dispatch."
proposals.reason: Chinese 高祖：「…」 is spoken dialogue; the literal line omits the verb of saying present in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: When High Ancestor reached the capital, Xian with Prince of Zhao Zhao both entered to bow in thanks.
proposals.after: When High Ancestor reached the capital, Xian with Zhao, Prince of Zhao, both entered to bow in thanks.
proposals.reason: The literal doubles the name as "Prince of Zhao Zhao," fusing title and given name unnaturally.

proposals.before: Moreover as the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, he always treated him with friendship and respect.
proposals.after: Moreover, because Zhi was the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, Xian always treated him with friendship and respect.
proposals.reason: Silent subject 帝之母弟 is Zhi (later 太后之子), while 每加友敬 is Xian's conduct; the English pronouns leave the pair reversed or ambiguous, conflicting with 異生 in s0091.

proposals.before: You are the empress dowager's son by partial favor and specially cherished.
proposals.after: You are the empress dowager's own son and have received her loving care in special measure.
proposals.reason: 親太后之子 marks own/biological son of the dowager; 偏荷慈愛 is special receipt of her affection, not "son by partial favor."

proposals.before: At the time Pillar-of-State Prince of Chen Chun halted the army at Thousand-Li Path; Grand General Yongchang Gong Chun encamped at Roosting-Chicken Plain; Grand General Yuwen Sheng held Fen River Pass—all under Xian's command.
proposals.after: At the time Pillar-of-State Chun, Prince of Chen, halted the army at Thousand-Li Path; Grand General Chun, Duke of Yongchang, encamped at Roosting-Chicken Plain; Grand General Yuwen Sheng held Fen River Pass—all under Xian's command.
proposals.reason: Yongchang Gong Chun leaves the noble title untranslated and collides with Prince of Chen Chun; both 純 and 椿 are romanized Chun and need distinct title order.

proposals.before: Yuwen Xian said: "I am only a great commander of Yu
proposals.after: Yuwen Xian said: "I am only the Yuhou Grand Commander
proposals.reason: The office is 虞候大都督 (yuhou dadudu), not a commander of a place called Yu.

proposals.before: Hou after all."
proposals.after: after all."
proposals.reason: 候 continues the office title 虞候大都督; Hou is not a personal name.

proposals.before: Yuwen Xian then said: "I am the Son of Heaven's elder brother, Prince of Qi."
proposals.after: Yuwen Xian then said: "I am the Son of Heaven's younger brother, Prince of Qi."
proposals.reason: 太弟 names the emperor's younger brother, not an elder brother.

proposals.before: Northern Qi forces besieged Jin Province day and night without cease.
proposals.after: The Northern Qi ruler besieged Jin Province day and night without cease.
proposals.reason: 齊主 is the Qi ruler in person, not generic Qi forces.

proposals.before: The next day he joined the great army at Jiezhou.
proposals.after: The next day he joined the great army at Jiexiu.
proposals.reason: 介休 is Jiexiu, not Jiezhou.

proposals.before: At the time the Northern Qi ruler had already fled to Ye; he left his cousin Prince of Ande Yan Zong to hold Bing Province.
proposals.after: At the time the Northern Qi ruler had already fled to Ye; he left his cousin Prince of Ande Yanzong to hold Bing Province.
proposals.reason: 延宗 is the single given name Yanzong rather than two words Yan Zong.

proposals.before: Northern Qi Prince of Rencheng Gao Ta, Prince of Guangning Xiao Heng, and others held and defended Xindu, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
proposals.after: Northern Qi Prince of Rencheng Gao Jie, Prince of Guangning Gao Xiaoheng, and others held and defended Xindu, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
proposals.reason: 湝 is Jie, not Ta; 孝珩 is Xiaoheng, not Xiao Heng as a split given name.

proposals.before: Qi Prince of Rencheng Ta, Prince of Guangning Xiao Heng, and others held and defended Xindu, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
proposals.after: Qi Prince of Rencheng Jie, Prince of Guangning Xiaoheng, and others held and defended Xindu, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
proposals.reason: Matches 湝 and 孝珩 rather than Ta and Xiao Heng.

proposals.before: He also had the Northern Qi ruler write in his own hand to Gao Ta, saying: "The court has treated the latitude of the realm with great kindness; the princes are unharmed.
proposals.after: He also had the Northern Qi ruler write in his own hand to Gao Jie, saying: "The court has treated Wei with great kindness; the princes are unharmed.
proposals.reason: 緯 is the Qi ruler's given name Wei, not latitude; 湝 is Jie.

proposals.before: He also had the Qi ruler write in his own hand to Ta, saying: "The court has treated the latitude of the realm with great kindness; the princes are unharmed.
proposals.after: He also had the Qi ruler write in his own hand to Jie, saying: "The court has treated Wei with great kindness; the princes are unharmed.
proposals.reason: Same correction of 緯 and 湝.

proposals.before: Yuwen Xian reached Xindu; Gao Rui drew up battle lines south of the city, and Yuwen Xian ascended Zhang Er's mound to observe them.
proposals.after: Yuwen Xian reached Xindu; Gao Jie drew up battle lines south of the city, and Yuwen Xian ascended Zhang Er's mound to observe them.
proposals.reason: The same 湝 is Jie throughout; Rui is a different character.

proposals.before: Xian reached Xindu; Rui drew up battle lines south of the city, and Xian ascended Zhang Er's mound to observe them.
proposals.after: Xian reached Xindu; Jie drew up battle lines south of the city, and Xian ascended Zhang Er's mound to observe them.
proposals.reason: Rui does not render 湝.

proposals.before: Before long Wei Xiangyuan, the camp commander Gao Rui had appointed, feigned going out to reconnoiter the lines and thereupon surrendered with his troops.
proposals.after: Before long Yu Xiangyuan, the Leader of the Army Gao Jie had appointed, feigned going out to reconnoiter the lines and thereupon surrendered with his troops.
proposals.reason: 尉 is the surname Yu, not Wei; 領軍 is Lingjun; 湝 remains Jie.

proposals.before: The next day they fought again; Yuwen Xian broke them, capturing and slaying thirty thousand men, and seized Gao Rui, Gao Xiaoyuan, and the others.
proposals.after: The next day they fought again; Yuwen Xian broke them, capturing and slaying thirty thousand men, and seized Gao Jie, Gao Xiaoheng, and the others.
proposals.reason: 湝 is Jie and 孝珩 is Xiaoheng, not Rui and Xiaoyuan.

proposals.before: The emperor thereupon sent Junior Tomb Director Yuwen Xiaobo to say to Yuwen Xian: "The Three Excellencies' posts should belong to close kin and the worthy; now we wish to make Uncle Grand Preceptor, Ninth Uncle Grand Tutor, and Eleventh Uncle Grand Protector—what does Uncle think?"
proposals.after: The emperor thereupon sent Junior Grand Steward Yuwen Xiaobo to say to Yuwen Xian: "The Three Excellencies' posts should belong to close kin and the worthy; now we wish to make Uncle Grand Preceptor, Ninth Uncle Grand Tutor, and Eleventh Uncle Grand Protector—what does Uncle think?"
proposals.reason: 小冢宰 is the junior grand steward / minister of state, not a tomb office; “Junior Tomb Director” invents a funerary sense from 冢.

proposals.before: The emperor thereupon sent Junior Tomb Director Yuwen Xiaobo to say to Xian: "The Three Excellencies' posts should belong to close kin and the worthy; now we wish to make Uncle Grand Preceptor, Ninth Uncle Grand Tutor, and Eleventh Uncle Grand Protector—what does Uncle think?"
proposals.after: The emperor thereupon sent Junior Grand Steward Yuwen Xiaobo to say to Xian: "The Three Excellencies' posts should belong to close kin and the worthy; now we wish to make Uncle Grand Preceptor, Ninth Uncle Grand Tutor, and Eleventh Uncle Grand Protector—what does Uncle think?"
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 小冢宰 as a tomb directorship in the literal English.

proposals.before: They also killed Grand General of the Upper Army Wang Xing, Duke of Anyi, Upper Opener-of-Gates Dugu Xiong, and Opener-of-Gates Doulu Shao—all because they were intimate with Yuwen Xian.
proposals.after: They also killed Senior Grand General Wang Xing, Duke of Anyi, Upper Opener-of-Gates Dugu Xiong, and Opener-of-Gates Doulu Shao—all because they were intimate with Yuwen Xian.
proposals.reason: 上大將軍 is the senior grand-general rank, not a ‘grand general of the Upper Army’.

proposals.before: Cong, styled Qianli, was grand general and Duke of Zhongao.
proposals.after: Cong, styled Qianli, was grand general and Duke of Zhongba.
proposals.reason: 中垻公 is Zhongba; Zhongao misreads 垻.

decisions.reason: 盜殺 records that Kongcheng garrison commander 能奔達 was killed; 以城應之 then says the city went over. The original relative clause makes the slain commander also flee and surrender the city by misreading 奔達 as verbs.

decisions.reason: The same clause 盜殺孔城防主能奔達 names the commander 能奔達; 奔達 is not ‘flee and reach.’ 以城應之 is the city’s going over after his death.

decisions.reason: The person is 新蔡王王康; 得以憲兵至 is the circumstance that Xian’s troops had arrived, not a given name Kangde. The replacement restores the name and keeps the temporal clause.
